overall_reason: A warm-paper default (cream page, orange accent, mono caps eyebrows on every section, 01/02/03 steps, icon-tile card grid, dark CTA band with decorative bars) carries copy built from 'X, not Y' pairs; the INR persona stacks are the only part that belongs to this product.

findings.evidence: Sections run: hero with eyebrow, 10 equal icon-tile goal cards, 'HOW IT WORKS' 01/02/03 steps, 3 equal persona cards, 'THE DIRECTORY' equal tool cards, 'READY WHEN YOU ARE' dark CTA band with three decorative bars, 3-column link footer. Stock items: equal feature cards, 1-2-3 steps, three-tier-style cards, CTA band, link-farm footer = 5 of the stock list in stock order.
findings.before: Hero > equal cards > 1-2-3 steps > three cards > card grid > CTA band > footer
findings.after: Let the goal picker be the page: answer question 1 inline and show the resulting stack on the same screen instead of explaining the flow in a separate 01/02/03 band.
findings.why: Specific words on a default skeleton still read as a default page; the 1-2-3 band repeats what the picker above it already shows.

findings.evidence: Negation-pair formula on four headings: 'AI tool stacks, not directories', 'A workflow, not a list. Built around you.', '23 hand-picked tools. No filler.', 'Stop collecting tools. Start using the right ones.'
findings.before: "A workflow, not a list. Built around you."
findings.after: State what the visitor gets, e.g. "Five tools, in order, with the monthly cost for each."
findings.why: The 'not X' and fragment-pair habit is the substitute tic that replaces adjectives in model copy; four in one page make it a pattern.

findings.evidence: Mono tracked caps eyebrow above every h2 ('HOW IT WORKS', 'SAME GOAL, DIFFERENT PEOPLE', 'THE DIRECTORY', 'READY WHEN YOU ARE'), plus a red dot bullet on the hero eyebrow; together with cream #f9f8f5 and orange #ee491b this is the warm-paper family the sweep counted.
findings.before: HOW IT WORKS / A workflow, not a list.
findings.after: Drop the eyebrows; keep 'Question 1 of 3', which is real state.
findings.why: Only one eyebrow carries information ('Question 1 of 3'); the rest are template chrome.

findings.evidence: 10 identical cards, each a grey rounded icon tile (mortarboard, play, pen, globe, rocket, shop, briefcase, newspaper, nodes, palette) over a title, one-line sub and arrow.
findings.before: Icon tile + 'Study smarter' + 'Research, notes and revision that stick' + arrow
findings.after: A plain list or segmented choice of goals; the icons add nothing the label does not say.
findings.why: Deleting the icon tiles loses no meaning; the rocket-for-SaaS, globe-for-website set is the stock icon vocabulary.

findings.evidence: Orange mono '01', '02', '03' over 'Share your goal', 'Set budget and skill', 'Get your workflow' in three equal cells.
findings.before: 01 Share your goal / 02 Set budget and skill / 03 Get your workflow
findings.after: Delete the band; the 'Question 1 of 3' picker already demonstrates the steps.
findings.why: Decorative step numbering on a three-step explainer is a default section.

findings.evidence: Dark rounded band 'Stop collecting tools. Start using the right ones.' with three decorative horizontal bars (orange, two greys) running off the right edge.
findings.before: Decorative bar graphic in CTA band
findings.after: Remove the bars, or replace them with a real stack result preview.
findings.why: The bars carry no data; deleting them loses nothing.

findings.evidence: Fresh-reader lines that fit any AI directory: 'A thoughtful AI assistant for long-form writing, analysis and code.', 'Beautiful presentations and docs, generated in seconds.', 'Let software do the busywork'.
findings.before: "Beautiful presentations and docs, generated in seconds."
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: what this site's curator found each tool best at, e.g. the task it was picked for in a stack]
findings.why: Vendor-tagline blurbs make the 'hand-picked' claim unverifiable.

strengths: The 'Same goal, different people' persona stacks are specific: student/no budget/doesn't code vs freelancer INR 500-2,000 vs developer, with monthly cost in rupees and a role for each tool. Keep these.
The footer note 'Prices are approximate monthly amounts in INR and may change' is honest and local.
Hero h1 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' answers what and what to do within five seconds.
not_investigated: Result pages (/results, /find): only the home page was captured.
The 'Edit with Base44' badge is platform chrome, not judged as design.
